notes.title: Messy Bonds: Writing Family in Crown of Exile
notes.content: [p]When we think about family arcs in interactive fiction, they often follow one of two neat paths: either everything is repaired with a single emotional conversation and everyone is happy again, or the bond is broken forever and there’s no space left to rebuild. Both are satisfying in their way — clear, simple, and easy for players to understand.[/p][p]But in [i]Crown of Exile[/i], I wanted something different. Families in real life don’t usually break or heal in such a clean way. They’re messy, complicated, and contradictory — and sometimes the most honest stories are the ones that sit in that uncomfortable middle ground.[/p][p][/p][h2]Siduri: The Glue of the Family 🪡[/h2][p]Siduri, the MC’s grandmother, is often described as the 'glue' holding the family together. She isn’t naïve; she knows the family she once dreamed of doesn’t exist anymore. But her desire for normalcy isn’t about pretending nothing happened — it’s about refusing to let grief and resentment be the only things her grandchildren inherit.[/p][p]She stitches the family back together in small ways, the same way she mends her son’s tunics: not to erase the wear and tear, but to keep things from falling apart completely. Her strength is quiet, her hope stubborn, and her love relentless.[/p][p]For Siduri, family isn’t about perfection — it’s about endurance.[/p][p][/p][h2]Salyra: A Mother in the Shadow of Guilt 🌒[/h2][p]Salyra, the MC’s mother, is harder to understand. Some players see her as cold, or even careless. After all, she left her child behind for twenty years — how can she just step back into their life as though nothing has changed?[/p][p]But Salyra’s behaviour comes from guilt and fear, not arrogance. She left to protect her child, and though her reasoning was born of love, the wound of her absence only deepened as the years passed. When faced with her grown child again, pretending their bond is intact is the only way she knows how to cope. To admit the distance would be to admit the pain she caused — and she doesn’t know how to carry that.[/p][p]In her heart, the love never vanished. She simply doesn’t know how to express it after so much time apart.[/p][p][/p][h2]Ahlf: Protecting His Child in a World of Shadows ⚓[/h2][p]Ahlf isn’t the warm, idealised father some players might expect. He’s gruff, blunt, and often unsure how to comfort a child who isn’t a soldier. His instincts tell him to protect, to scold, to teach resilience — sometimes harshly. And yet, even in the midst of frustration, tenderness leaks through: a guiding hand, a patient direction, a quiet acknowledgement that love doesn’t always come with the right words.[/p][p]He teaches through action rather than speech: mending nets, gutting fish, tending the home, and showing that survival itself is an act of care. His child learns the same lessons that shaped him — resourcefulness, resilience, and the subtle, enduring bond of family.[/p][p][/p][h2]Player Agency: No Easy Resolutions 🎭[/h2][p]This is where the MC — and the player — comes in. In [i]Crown of Exile[/i], you aren’t forced into reconciliation, nor are you locked into permanent estrangement. The choices you make shape how (or if) these bonds are rebuilt.[/p][p]Some players will decide their MC cannot forgive Salyra. Others may let Siduri’s quiet persistence inspire them to try. And some may choose a middle path — acknowledging the pain but keeping the door open for future healing.[/p][p]There’s no single “right” answer, because families rarely give us easy answers.[/p][p][/p][h2]Why It Matters ✨[/h2][p][i]Crown of Exile[/i] is a story about war, survival, and legacy — but it’s also about how love and family endure even when fractured. By writing Siduri, Salyra and Ahlf the way I have, I wanted to reflect the messy, bittersweet truth: that bonds don’t snap cleanly, and they don’t mend instantly either. They stretch, fray, and knot themselves back together in uneven, imperfect ways.[/p][p]For me, that’s more powerful than a tidy resolution. And for players, it creates a space to explore how [i]they[/i] believe family should be handled in a world defined by loss.[/p][p]Because sometimes, the bravest thing a character can do isn’t fighting a war — it’s sitting at a table with someone they love, and choosing to try again.[/p]

notes.title: 🌍 Dive Into the World of Crown of Exile – Meet the Kingdoms
notes.content:
[p]To celebrate all the love and support since the launch of our Steam page, I wanted to share a bit of the world you’ll be stepping into when [i]Crown of Exile[/i] releases. Here's a peek at the three major regions shaping the world—and the fate of your character.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45686364/17f8934ce99b9baadba8f956368d782076147d65.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][h3]🟡 [b]Cyre – “Conquered by None”[/b][/h3][p]Once a sprawling, united kingdom, Cyre now teeters between tradition and tyranny. Once a place of diverse beliefs, it now enforces worship of a single god—Solus—under royal decree. With eight major cities and a Mediterranean climate, Cyre is a land of golden feasts, sun temples, and simmering rebellion.[/p][list][*][p][b]Population[/b]: 50–80 million[/p][/*][*][p][b]Religion[/b]: Monotheistic worship of Solus; ancient gods worshipped in secret[/p][/*][*][p][b]Cuisine[/b]: Coastal seafood, spiced dishes, and seasonal feasts[/p][/*][*][p][b]Symbol[/b]: A ringed sun, representing Solus’s reach[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][h3]🟢 [b]Vinia – “Strength in Unity”[/b][/h3][p]Bordering Cyre to the south, Vinia is a neutral, multicultural kingdom. It's become a haven for those fleeing Cyre’s religious crackdowns. Its 15 major cities range from tundra outposts to bustling trade ports, and it welcomes all faiths—from the Ancient Ones to the Twelve.[/p][list][*][p][b]Population[/b]: 80–100 million[/p][/*][*][p][b]Religion[/b]: Open practice of any belief system[/p][/*][*][p][b]Cuisine[/b]: Spiced, dairy-rich, and diverse thanks to major trade routes[/p][/*][*][p][b]Symbol[/b]: Three spirals joined in a cosmic circle, symbolising universal connection[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h3]🔴 [b]Ishari – “Risen to the Stars”[/b][/h3][p]Once a city under Cyre’s domain, Ishari won its freedom in a civil war known as the Battle of the Bridge. Built between three rivers and fiercely spiritual, Ishari remains the last sanctuary of the Ancient Ones, with a culture shaped by sacrifice, star-worship, and survival.[/p][list][*][p][b]Population[/b]: ~80,000 before independence; ~10,000 after[/p][/*][*][p][b]Religion[/b]: Polytheistic worship of the Ancient Ones[/p][/*][*][p][b]Cuisine[/b]: Rich in grains, spiced vegetables and meats[/p][/*][*][p][b]Symbol[/b]: A serpent beneath the stars—life descending from the cosmos[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]✨This is just the beginning of the worldbuilding you’ll experience. Every kingdom has secrets, and every region has its cost. Who will you trust—and where will your loyalties lie?[/p][p]➡️ [i]Follow along for more lore reveals and dev updates![/i]
💬 Feel free to ask questions or share your favourite kingdom in the comments![/p]

notes.title: 🌸 The Calm After the Launch 🌸
notes.content:
[p]Hello everyone![/p][p][/p][p]It’s been just under a week since [i]Crown of Exile[/i] launched its Steam store page, and I’m still reeling (in the best way possible). Thank you to everyone who has supported the game so far by wishlisting, sharing, and leaving lovely words of encouragement. 💖[/p][p][/p][p]If you haven’t already, please consider adding [i]Crown of Exile[/i] to your wishlist. Every wishlist helps signal to Steam that more people might want to see this game, and that helps [i]a lot[/i] as a solo indie dev.[/p][p][/p][p]🪻 [i]Crown of Exile[/i] is a grounded political fantasy interactive fiction story about betrayal, legacy, and the weight of power. Your choices shape the world around you — from the battlefield to the throne room, and from the people you lead to those you love.[/p][p][/p][h2]💌 Want to follow along or support development?[/h2][list][*][p]✨ [url="https://www.patreon.com/ramonag_if"]Join me on Patreon[/url] for behind-the-scenes devlogs, exclusive side stories, and early content.[/p][/*][*][p]🌿 [url="https://www.tumblr.com/ramonag-if"]Follow the game on Tumblr[/url] for character aesthetics, sneak peeks, and interactive posts.[/p][/*][*][p]📜 [url="https://mona-mae.itch.io/crown-of-exile"]Play the free demo on itch.io[/url] — up to Chapter Eight available.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]Thank you again for being here. This is only the beginning, and I’m so excited to share what comes next.[/p][p]
Ramona 🌸[/p][p][/p][p][b]PS: Which story element are you most drawn to in games: romance, strategy, moral choices... or all of the above? I’d love to hear what keeps you turning the page (or clicking the next choice).[/b][/p]

notes.title: The Crown Has Been Claimed: Crown of Exile Is Now on Steam
notes.content:
[h1][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45686364/a06b9056a9f7bdaf709e9cc1325fa7c95923f1ee.png"][/img][i][b]Crown of Exile[/b][/i][b] is now live on Steam.[/b][/h1][p][/p][h3]In a world where thrones are lost and loyalties fracture like glass, [i]Crown of Exile[/i] finally steps into the light. Wield influence, bear betrayal, and decide who you become when the world unravels. Your path is yours to carve, but power always has a price.[/h3][p][/p][h3]After years of writing, revising, and weaving choice into consequence, I’m so proud (and a little nervous!) to unveil the official [b]Steam Store Page[/b] for my debut interactive fiction game.[/h3][p][/p][h3][b]♦ One million+ words[/b]
♦ [b]Unforgiving politics[/b]
♦ [b]Divinity. Betrayal. Survival.[/b][/h3][h3][/h3][h3]If you’ve ever wanted to rule, run, or simply endure. This is a story shaped by your decisions, not fate.[/h3][p][/p][h2]► Click [url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/2715550/Crown_of_Exile/?beta=0" buttoncolor="#ff0026"][b]here[/b][/url][url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/2715550/Crown_of_Exile/?beta=0" buttoncolor="#ff0026"] [/url]to wishlist [i]Crown of Exile[/i][/h2][p][/p][h3]Your support, even just a wishlist, makes a real difference and helps more players discover the story.[/h3]
